name: Parking garage
summary: Freestanding above-grade structured parking is well benchmarked: WGI's annual Parking Structure Cost Outlook (national median of hundreds of completed garages) is the anchor, with RLB-based city averages (UCLA ITS 2026) and a recent public design-build contract showing the upper range. Cost is driven by efficiency (SF per space), structural system, facade, sprinklers/EV mandates and market; below-grade parking is excluded and roughly 1.4x+ more expensive.

typicalSize.method: Municipal/institutional garages seen in this research range from ~450 spaces (Frisco Rail District, e5) to 1,000+; mid 600 is a typical stand-alone municipal/campus garage. Judgment, verify per project.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Implied gross SF per space from WGI medians: 2026 $33,300 / $98.75 = 337 SF; 2024 $29,900 / $89.45 = 334 SF; Houston 2026 $27,806 / $82.46 = 337 SF. Low/high +/- ~7% for efficient long-span vs. constrained sites.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Footprint ~ 43,560 SF x 0.8 usable / 337 SF per space = ~100 spaces per level per acre; 3-7 supported levels -> ~300-700 spaces per acre of site. Mid assumes ~4.5 levels.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Mid = WGI 2026 national median $33,300/space (e1), hard construction only. Low = WGI's lowest-cost major market, Houston, $27,806 (e1). High = UCLA ITS / RLB 2025 17-city average for above-ground structures, $52,000 (e4), corroborated by Frisco TX 451-space design-build contract at ~$52,900/space incl. ground-floor retail shell (e5); San Francisco $43,000 (e1) sits between. UCLA figure is 2025 dollars (within 1 year of 2026). RLB Q3 2026 'Parking — Ground' city ranges (e8) have a median midpoint of ~$165/SF (~$55.6k/space), i.e., core-city consultant ranges sit near the high value; WGI's completed-project median is kept as the national mid because it covers suburban/campus garages too.

perSF.method: WGI 2026 median $98.75/SF (e1); low = Houston $82.46/SF (e1); high = $52,000/space (e4) / 337 SF per space = ~$154/SF. RLB 2026 city median midpoint ~$165/SF (e8) supports the high.

scope.notes: WGI medians are construction cost only (contractor price) for open, naturally ventilated precast or CIP above-grade garages with shallow foundations, standard LED lighting, conventional PARCS; excludes land, A/E, testing, permits, financing. WGI notes most garages in its database predate 2021 IBC so the median 'generally does not reflect' full sprinklers, and EV spaces were only 1-2% (e3) — add those via line items.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = Houston/median (27,806/33,300 = 0.84). Premium ~ San Francisco/median (43,000/33,300 = 1.29) rounded down to 1.25 for architectural facade/curtain-wall stairs. Luxury = RLB 17-city above-ground average/median (52,000/33,300 = 1.56).

systemSplit.method: No public elemental breakdown for a garage was found. Derived for a typical precast/CIP open garage (WGI 'median-cost' description, e3): structure (03) dominates at ~55%; general conditions/fee 8% (RSMeans model shows contractor fees of 25% on its subtotal, e7, but our baseline already includes OH&P throughout, so only GC is carried in 01); elevators 2 cars ~4%; drainage/plumbing 3%; dry sprinkler/standpipe 3%; lighting/power 6%; PARCS/security 2%; foundations/earthwork 5%; site paving/landscape 2%; utilities 1%. Verify against a bid tab.

lineItems.name: Full dry-pipe sprinkler system (2021 IBC trigger: >48,000 SF footprint or >55 ft)

cost.method: WGI states its median generally does not reflect a fully sprinklered garage (e3). Dry-pipe systems in unheated garages typically price ~$3.5-8/SF of garage floor; mid $5/SF is an estimating judgment, not a sourced figure — verify with a fire-protection sub.

lineItems.notes: Switch on where 2021+ IBC applies (large footprints or tall garages).

lineItems.name: EV charging — Level 2 port incl. conduit, panel capacity, install

cost.method: WGI notes EV mandates can reach 25% (commercial) to 100% (multifamily) of spaces vs. 1-2% historically (e3), so EV is outside the median. Per-port cost is an estimating judgment for networked L2 with conduit/transformer share; qty default 10% of spaces. Verify locally.

lineItems.notes: Set qty to the local EV-capable/EV-installed mandate.

lineItems.name: Passenger elevators (typically 2 cars per stair/elevator core)

cost.method: Carve-out of the 04% division-14 share in systemSplit: 0.04 x $33,300 x 600 spaces = ~$800k for a typical garage, i.e., ~2-3 cars at ~$225k-400k incl. glass-backed cab and hoistway. Shown for reference only.

lineItems.notes: Already inside the baseline per-space cost.

lineItems.name: Parking access & revenue control (PARCS) — gated entry/exit lanes

cost.method: WGI's median garage includes a 'conventional parking access and revenue-control system' (e3). Per-lane cost (gate, ticket/LPR, pay station share) is an estimating judgment; qty = 1 entry + 1 exit lane.

lineItems.notes: Inside the baseline; upgrade to LPR/ticketless adds modestly.

lineItems.name: Below-grade / podium parking premium (per space)

cost.method: UCLA ITS / RLB 2025: underground average $73,000/space vs above-ground $52,000/space (e4) -> ~$21,000 premium per space. Low/high reflect the wide city spread ($40k-$111k underground). Set qty = share of spaces below grade.

lineItems.notes: WGI excludes underground and beneath-building garages from its median (e1).

lineItems.name: Ground-floor retail liner shell (cold dark shell)

cost.method: Garages with ground-floor retail (e.g., Frisco, e5) carry a shell premium over garage SF; $/SF is an estimating judgment for storefront shell with MEP stub-outs. Enter retail SF as qty.

lineItems.notes: TI for the retail space is separate (see interior-finish-out).

pctOfHard.method: WGI: soft costs 'typically add about 15% to 25%' to construction cost (e2, e6). Mid = midpoint.

softCosts.notes: A/E for repetitive precast garages commonly runs ~5-7% (RSMeans model applies 6% architectural fees, e7). Design-build delivery is common for municipal garages.

design.method: Simple, repetitive building type -> low end of typical design contingency norms (judgment).

hard.method: Typical owner construction contingency for new structured parking; 10% used where geotech/foundation risk is high (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $27.8k x 1.15 soft = ~$32k (rounded to $30k); hard high $52k x 1.25 soft x 1.10 contingency = ~$72k, rounded up to $80k for EV/sprinkler-mandated coastal markets. Below-grade parking can exceed this.

evidence.region: United States (national median; Houston low, San Francisco high)

source.title: Parking structure construction cost up 6% in 2026
source.publisher: Building Design + Construction (reporting WGI 2026 Parking Structure Cost Outlook)

evidence.quote: The median structure construction cost reached $33,300 per space, or $98.75 per square foot ... San Francisco remains the nation's highest-cost market at $43,000 per space and $126.40 per square foot ... Houston ... $27,806 per space and $82.46 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Hard construction cost of above-grade parking structures; underground excluded.

source.title: WGI's Parking Structure Cost Outlook for 2024 (PDF)

evidence.quote: As of May 2024, our statistical data indicate that the median construction cost for a new parking structure is $29,900 per space, or $89.45 per square foot ... Soft costs typically add about 15% to 25% to the actual construction costs.
evidence.scopeNotes: Excludes land, A/E fees, environmental, testing, inspections, geotech, financing, owner admin/legal, permitting. Below-grade structures omitted as outliers.

source.title: WGI's Parking Structure Cost Outlook for 2024 (PDF)

evidence.quote: while our analysis does include fire-sprinklered facilities, the median cost generally does not reflect the cost of a fully sprinklered garage ... EV spaces historically made up only 1% to 2% of the total, at most.
evidence.scopeNotes: Median-cost garage typically includes precast superstructure and facade, glass-backed elevators, shallow foundations, all above grade, open naturally ventilated, conventional PARCS, LED lighting.

source.title: New report: No such thing as free parking
source.publisher: UCLA Institute of Transportation Studies (using 2025 Rider Levett Bucknall cost data)

evidence.quote: Aboveground parking structures cost, on average, $52,000 per space, with costs ranging from $29,000 in Phoenix, Arizona and Washington, D.C., to $99,000 in Portland, Oregon.
evidence.scopeNotes: Excludes land. Underground averages ~$73,000/space ($40k DC to $111k Portland). Derived from RLB $/SF ranges x SF/space, likely skewed to high-cost core cities.

source.title: Frisco sets construction date for Rail District parking garage

evidence.quote: $23.86 million lump sum ... 451 parking spaces ... five stories ... retail space available on a portion of the ground floor.
evidence.scopeNotes: Design-build (McCarthy) construction lump sum $23.86M / 451 spaces = $52,905/space (our arithmetic); includes ground-floor retail shell; earlier design work brings total to $26.01M. Approved Jan 7, 2025.

source.title: WGI releases 2026 parking structure cost outlook

evidence.scopeNotes: Soft costs on top of hard construction cost per WGI 2026; also reports 2025 median $31,400/space.

source.title: Parking Garage — RSMeans square foot model

evidence.quote: Cast in Place Concrete, 145,000 S.F., 5 stories: Contractor fees 25% $13.92; Architectural fees 6% $4.17; Total building cost $73.75 (union) / $65.16 (open shop)
evidence.scopeNotes: 2019 RSMeans model, includes 6% architectural fees (soft) inside total; used only for fee structure context, not for the default.

evidence.region: 18 U.S. cities (RLB indicative ranges; median of city midpoints)

source.title: RLB Construction Cost Report North America Q3 2026 (PDF), Indicative Construction Costs — Parking: Ground

evidence.quote: Indicative Construction Costs table, PARKING GROUND column (USD/SF GFA): Dallas 120-200; Chicago 105-155; New York 125-220; Phoenix 60-125; Washington, D.C. 75-100; San Francisco 140-210; Portland 290-340
evidence.scopeNotes: Hard construction cost per SF of gross floor area for above-ground ('ground') structured parking; basement parking is a separate column (e.g., Dallas 170-275). Median of the 18 US city midpoints = ~$165/SF (our arithmetic) -> ~$55,600/space at 337 SF. Core-city cost-consultant ranges run well above WGI's completed-project median.
